newsitem.title: YUGOSLAVIA: Serbia's judges split on election dispute.
newsitem.headline: Serbia's judges split on election dispute.

text.p: Five top Serbian judges accused their colleagues in the Supreme Court of being "subservient" to President Slobodan Milosevic in backing him in the dispute over municipal election results.

The 36-member Supreme Court rejected an appeal by the Zajedno opposition whose victories in local elections more than two weeks ago were annulled by electoral commissions citing unspecified "irregularities".

The five, members themselves of the Supreme Court, said in letters published on Tuesday in the independent Belgrade daily Nasa Borba that some members of the judiciary had taken part in electoral fraud by their action.

"The Serbian Supreme Court has unfortunately not had the strength and the courage to acknowledge to the electorate what belongs to it on the basis of election results," the paper quoted Judge Zoran Ivosevic as writing.
"I do not accept the subservient role of the court which turns elections into self-appointment," Ivosevic wrote.
"I do not agree to defend the state from democracy because democracy has to be defended from the state if it has not risen up to it," he wrote.

The responsibilities of Supreme Court judges are divided into criminal, civil and administrative law. The judges who wrote the letter are all civil law judges, while it was administrative judges ruled on the election results.
Responding to Zajedno claims that the socialists robbed the opposition of election victory, the judges wrote to Nasa Borba that their profession should not be associated with theft.
"If it is determined that there are such judges in our ranks then their place is not among us and we disassociate ourselves from them completely," they added.
Nasa Borba said the joint letter had also been sent to the state-run daily Politika which did not publish it.
Milosevic's socialists have already cracked down on independent media, jamming radio B-92's signal and journalists at state papers have complained of censorship.
